name: Tumakuru
headline: Fee affordability and child exploitation cases; Madhugiri lost hundreds of students to unorganised labour.
summary: Tumakuru sources include an SSLC girl who attempted suicide because her family could not pay exam fees, a police case after 24 runaway children alleged forced labour and abuse at a madrasa, and an older report that Madhugiri taluk lost 436 students to unorganised work.

reasons.factor: Hall ticket withheld over school fees
reasons.detail: In 2021 a Tumakuru Class 10 girl who scored 95% in Class 9 was not issued an SSLC hall ticket because she could not pay the school's fee; she attempted suicide and later topped the supplementary exams.
Police registered cases after 24 runaway children alleged abuse and forced labour at a madrasa in Tumakuru Rural.
A statewide dropout report listed Madhugiri with hundreds of students leaving to work in the unorganised sector.

A September 2026 statewide inspection drive found 33 children working in Tumakuru and handed them to the Child Welfare Committee. Their schooling status was not reported; state-level commentary ties child labour to poverty, migration and school access.

In 2025 about one in three Tumakuru SSLC candidates did not pass (67.03 percent pass, 20th in the state). Exam failure is a recognised exit point, but no source here links it to Tumakuru dropout directly.

A Deccan Herald report on a minister's visit described border-area schools, including Pavagada, hit by teacher shortages, dilapidated buildings, poor drinking water and improper toilets. Undated in the result and older; current position unverified.
State-level reporting on UDISE+ 2023-24 attributes Karnataka's high secondary dropout to secondary schools not growing in step with primary schools. This is not a Tumakuru-specific finding.
